stated_limitation: One caveat worth stating plainly is that LGd is not perfectly untuned. A substantial minority of LGd units reach significance, and the GLM's direction term helps there too; the thalamus in this dataset carries a weak orientation bias, and the LGd-to-VISp difference is one of degree, though a large one.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000021 (Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels) with simultaneous LGd/VISp/HVA recordings is the canonical dataset for demonstrating orientation selectivity in mouse visual cortex.
justification.handling: Real data streamed from S3 with explicit Allen default QC criteria, non-overlapping response windows asserted, and correct trial/TF alignment.
justification.analysis: Uses proper circular statistics, a permutation null that redoes preferred-TF selection inside each shuffle, cross-validated GLM and decoder, and an independent static-grating cross-check.
justification.correctness: Reported values reproduce from committed code, are internally consistent with the CSVs and figures, and rest on sound cross-validated and permutation-based statistics with large n.
justification.figures: Figures are well-labeled with units and sample sizes and clearly show the LGd-to-VISp emergence of tuning, the two-stimulus preference agreement, and the 180-degree decoder confusion signature.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up prominently names the specific LGd caveat and honestly explains the significant-but-tiny LGd p-value, with only a minor overstatement in one control-panel title.
justification.verdict: This is publication-quality autonomous work I would accept and build on with no required fixes.
